criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Every frame is a rendered place, and eight of nine share one stormFront Panhandle afternoon: cured grass, a red caprock in haze and a low western light. Frame 7 is the best frame. The two galvanized tubes on cribbing measure about 815 px and 1337 px on the PNG, a ratio of 1.64, which matches c15, and they sit on real contact shadows. The detail fails the zoom test in several places. The camera heads on frames 1, 3 and 6 are primitive boxes. On frame 6 the 33 heads on the rail are small blocks that can't be counted at full size, let alone at 432 px. The Texan on frame 9 is a low-poly mannequin with a mask-like face, and she is that frame's focal point. The mesa texture on frames 1 and 6 is streaked and smeared. Frames 4 and 5 are a blank sheet and a binder on a desk in a dark room with little sense of place. On frame 8 the hook and dek sit on a flat brown wall band that works as a plate. The deck is competent, but more than one frame leans on a primitive model, so it sits below the 7 descriptor.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The contact sheet reads as one deck: one sky preset, one light from the west-southwest, one grass and caprock ground, and one hero mast recurring on frames 1, 3, 6, 7 and 9, with the caliche road running from frame 1 to the gate on frame 9. Frames 4 and 5 are a deliberate held camera with the page swapped. The storyboard declares three continuity devices and a value cut at frame 8, and the render shows it. Frame 8 has a mean of 43.3 against about 68 to 73 everywhere else, and it is the only frame without the hero. deck_coherence and deck_chassis both passed. The interiors on frames 4, 5 and 8 sit a little outside the world, and the heads' 'motif evolution' can't be read at feed size.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces to a claim. I checked 33 and 34, 24, 26, $10,537,400, $6,423,554 and 64.04% (recomputed 4,113,846 / 6,423,554 = 0.6404), July 10, 2025, May 1st, 57463, 57941, 30 days and eight of 160. The quotes on frames 4, 5 and 6 match the snapshots I read character for character: 57941_7 page 13 metric 10, and the 57463_108 order line j. The first comment's count of 'six official records' is right. The absence is scoped carefully ('that line', 'A missing count isn't a count of none'), and I found no detection count anywhere else in the report. REFUTATIONS, none rising to a hard fail. (1) Authorship of the question. The cover says 'Asked for fire detections', frame 4 says 'The state wrote the question down' and frame 1 says 'The state's order asks'. The order's own FoF 50 says these are 'The evaluation metrics and criteria in SPS's application, as modified by the terms of the agreement', and FoF 51 says 'Under the agreement, SPS will use the agreed-upon evaluation metrics'. The metric came from SPS's application or the settlement it signed, not from the state asking. A reader believes the state asked and the utility dodged. The record says the utility agreed to count detections and then counted cameras. That is looser than the source in a way that changes who the reader thinks set the question. (2) Scope blur at the close. The resiliency plan and the report fall under 16 TAC 25.62. The 30-day intervention window on frame 9 and in the caption, and the 'Suggested' blueprint on frame 8, belong to 25.60 wildfire mitigation plans, a different plan type. The deck never says so. A reader will take the 30 days as a way into this SPS matter, and Docket 57463 closed in July 2025. (3) Journalism instead of a primary source. The Smokehouse Creek cause and 'largest in Texas history' on frame 2, and the eight of 160 on frame 8, rest on the Tribune. The frames attribute them, but a primary record exists (the Forest Service finding, the hearing record). (4) Sources block labels. c32, c33 and c34 are listed under 'Item 108, filing receipt', but they come from the Order body. c28 (testimony) and c29 (the 1898 study) are listed under 'plan section 2.1.d'. The block also prints 'April 17, 2026', 'September 21, 2026' and 'December 30, 2024' without the ordinal, and the first two carry the post's own year. Those are citation labels generated by sources_block, so I did not make them a hard fail, but they break the house date rule in published LinkedIn copy.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: What happened, who decided and the document trail are clear. The PUCT approved the plan on July 10, 2025, SPS filed on May 1st and the detections line says cameras. Frame 2 gives the stakes concretely with Smokehouse Creek and SPS's own 'two ignitions' testimony. The 'where' is only 'Texas Panhandle', and texan_check warns that no county is named, even though the claims hold Moore County (c54) and Hutchinson County (c55). The action on frame 9 is generic. It tells the reader to search two dockets, one of them closed, and quotes a 30-day window for 'a utility's wildfire plan case' without naming SPS's own wildfire plan filing or a date. The claims hold a real dated next step, the next annual report due May 1 under the rule (c6), and SPS says full-year data will come in its 2027 report. The deck never uses either. A Texan can't tell what they can still act on.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe with 'Asked for fire detections. Counted cameras.' Frame 2 pays at once with the fire. The turn on frames 4 to 5, the same camera with the page swapped, is well built, and frame 7's 'The cost was counted to the dollar' is a sharp counterpoint. Frame 6 restates frame 5's finding with a new picture and could be cut with little loss. Frame 8 detours to statewide wildfire-plan compliance under a different rule with no bridge sentence, then frame 9 lands on a generic procedural close rather than a stake.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Restrained, specific and fair. 'A missing count isn't a count of none.' and 'The cost was counted to the dollar.' are strong, and the utility's partial-year caveat is carried on frame 5 and in the caption. I found no banned words, colons outside verbatim quotes, dashes or 'cannot'. There are flat lines. Frame 8's dek, 'The Tribune reports that count of utilities in fire-prone areas reached lawmakers at a House State Affairs hearing on the wildfire plan law', reads as clumsy wire copy. The Texas detail lives in the art (caprock, caliche), while the copy stays at 'Texas Panhandle' and never names a town or county.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The topic is new. No wildfire, utility or PUCT resiliency deck appears in the 30-day topics ledger, so there is no repeat. The storyboard says the stormFront world is new to the last four decks. The spine is again what a document does not say, and the ledger has asked the next run in capitals, from nos. 11, 14, 15, 16, 23 and 28, for a spine that is a thing somebody did. The cover's opening move is that same absence. 'AI cameras watching Texans' also sits seven days after no. 31, Dallas AI cameras, and twenty days after no. 18, Austin cameras.

one_sentence_fix: Rewrite the cover, frame 1's dek and frame 4 so they say what the order actually says, that counting detections was one of the metrics 'in SPS's application, as modified by the terms of the agreement' (FoF 50 and 51) and that SPS agreed to it and then counted cameras, and replace frame 9's generic 25.60 intervention window with the dated next step in this very matter, the next annual report due May 1st (c6) and SPS's own promise of full-year data in its 2027 report, naming Moore or Hutchinson County on the way.
